original_forecast.resolution_rule: Use the first U.S. Department of Labor Unemployment Insurance Weekly Claims release published 2026-09-03 at 08:30 ET for the week ended 2026-08-29. Resolve TRUE if the advance seasonally adjusted initial-claims level is 215000 or higher; otherwise FALSE. Score p=0.23 with Brier and log loss. Score the 207000 point estimate by absolute error against the same first-release level and against the frozen point benchmarks. Record whether the 194000-220000 80% interval contains the first-release value. Do not substitute later revisions.
rationale: ADP's +38K August private-payroll reading and July JOLTS weak hires reinforce a low-hiring regime, but neither directly measures separation flow.
Initial claims were only 203K in the latest release and have remained mostly in the low-200K range, so the model still assigns below-base-rate probability to an immediate jump to >=215K.

The threshold is intentionally chosen as a discriminating intermediate test: a rise to >=215K would indicate that weak labor demand is beginning to propagate into layoffs, strengthening H002 more than weak hiring alone.
The point estimate is slightly above the frozen consensus/no-change benchmarks to reflect accumulating weak-hiring evidence without conflating ADP payroll growth with layoffs.
surprising_if: Initial claims are >=225000, which would be materially stronger evidence of layoff transmission than the current low-hire/low-fire model expects.
Initial claims are <=195000 despite weak ADP hiring, reinforcing a pronounced hiring/separation divergence and reducing near-term H002 layoff-transmission probability.
source_notes: Department of Labor Aug. 27 first release: 203K initial claims for week ended Aug. 22 and 205.5K four-week average.
ADP Sep. 2 report: +38K private payrolls in August; distinct from BLS payrolls and not used as a direct claims proxy.
Investing calendar snapshot captured at cutoff: 205K consensus for the Sep. 3 initial-claims release.

resolution.source: U.S. Department of Labor, Unemployment Insurance Weekly Claims, first release published 2026-09-03 at 08:30 ET for week ended 2026-08-29.
resolution.audit_note: Forecast content above is preserved without hindsight alteration. The first-release initial-claims level was 206K, so the >=215K event resolved FALSE. The 0.23 probability produced Brier 0.0529 and log loss 0.261365, beating both the neutral 0.50 comparator and the frozen recent-10-release p=0.30 comparator on this outcome. The 207K point estimate missed by 1K: it beat the 203K no-change point by 2K of absolute error, tied the frozen 205K calendar consensus at 1K error, and lost to the frozen 205.5K four-week-average point benchmark by 0.5K. The 206K outcome fell inside the 194K-220K 80% interval. This is positive out-of-sample evidence for the specific low-hire/low-fire separation-flow decomposition, but one claims release does not establish broad model learning or rule out deterioration in the official monthly employment report.
